newsitem.title: USA: Liability issue key in tobacco talks - NY Times.
newsitem.headline: Liability issue key in tobacco talks - NY Times.

text.p: Negotiations between state attorneys general and the tobacco industry may be hitting a snag over the question of liability for smoking-related claims, the New York Times said.
Citing people familiar with the talks, the Times said in its Monday edition that state attorneys general were becoming increasingly divided over the liability issue.

Talks with the industry have been taking place in Dallas. And people involved in those negotiations told the Times that a wide gulf existed between the states and the tobacco industry over issues, such as the types of lawsuits smokers could bring and the amount of money they could collect.

"Nobody has made any concessions," said Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal, who heads the attorneys general's committee on civil liability. "Liablility is the key issue, and we have decided that there is no point taking on any of the other issues until we are able to resolve it."
In the talks, which began last month, cigarette producers initially proposed submitting to regulation by the Food and Drug Administration and creating a settlement fund that could total $300 billion.
In return, cigarette producers sought to shield themselves from present and future liability claims from smokers.
Spokesmen for Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, two tobacco giants participating in the talks, declined to comment in the Timese on the status of the negotiations.
